title: Sonnets and Haiku

concepts.def: Turn in argument inside a sonnet.

walkthroughs.body_html: A sonnet has 14 lines in iambic pentameter. The Shakespearean form is 3 quatrains then a couplet; rhyme ABABCDCDEFEFGG.
The volta is the turn in argument — often line 9 (Italian) or before the final couplet (Shakespearean). It shifts the poem's idea.
A haiku has 3 lines of 5, 7, 5 syllables. It captures a moment, often in nature.

mcqs.q: A sonnet has how many lines?
A haiku has the syllable pattern.
What is the difference between a theme and a symbol?
options: Dramatic irony is when characters speak in dramatic voices.
A theme is an abstract idea or concern the text explores (e.g. mortality); a symbol is a concrete image that stands for something else (e.g. a skull).
Themes are just symbols repeated through the book.
A theme is the title of the book.

mcqs.q: What is the dramatic function of a soliloquy?
options: Dramatic irony is when characters speak in dramatic voices.
A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
It reveals a character's inner thoughts directly to the audience while the character is alone on stage — a convention granting access to private psychology.
A soliloquy is any long speech a character gives.
Dramatic irony is when characters speak in dramatic voices.
When the audience knows something a character does not, creating tension between the character's words/actions and the audience's understanding.
A theme is the title of the book.
Dramatic irony is when something ironic happens in a play.
